position.summary: According to the text, Israel was navigating two simultaneous security shocks ahead of the October 27 election: the FlyDubai cockpit attack involving an Omani copilot and Israeli passengers returning from Dubai, and the revelation that Egypt had warned Netanyahu before the October 7, 2023 attack. Netanyahu's secret Abu Dhabi visit, in which he reportedly shared new intelligence on Iran's nuclear program with Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed, underscored deepening Gulf-Israel coordination even as the UAE and Saudi Arabia adopted cautious public stances. The Netherlands revoked Israeli diplomats' accreditation over settlement sanctions, the ZIM/Hapag-Lloyd shipping deal was halted due to Saudi and Qatari ownership stakes, and the Supreme Court's indication prompted the withdrawal of Sami Abu Shehadeh, tightening the legal battle over Arab party eligibility. In Gaza, the death toll exceeded 74,000 with strikes ongoing in what the text called a long grinding conflict. West Bank settlers marched between settlements during Sukkot, blocking families and seizing water sources. The Irish national football team wore black armbands and skipped handshakes against Israel, while Hapoel Beer-Sheva lost its away fans in two Europa League matches. Trump threatened Iran with a very hard response if evidence linked it to the cockpit incident. The overall mood was one of a nation caught between projecting strength and answering for its failures.

key_events.event: The FlyDubai cockpit attack involving an Omani copilot and Israeli passengers from Dubai shook national security confidence.
Leaks revealed that Egypt had warned Netanyahu before the October 7, 2023 attack, igniting a political fight over the security establishment's preparedness.
Netanyahu secretly visited Abu Dhabi and reportedly shared new intelligence on Iran's nuclear program with Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed.
The Netherlands revoked Israeli diplomats' accreditation over settlement sanctions and the ZIM/Hapag-Lloyd shipping deal was halted over Gulf ownership stakes.
Gaza's war entered its third year with the death toll above 74,000 and strikes still falling across the territory.
